method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, constructor-by-constructor replay of the recursive definition, verification of the occurrence example and table, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Definition, existence, uniqueness and classification uses of a formula's main operator.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A formula's main operator is the last operator used in its construction, intuitively its outermost operator; negation and disjunction illustrate the idea.
samples.checks: The last-used, outermost and formula-specific senses and both examples are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Atomic formulas have no main operator. Each selected unary, binary or quantified constructor has the displayed operator as its main operator.
samples.checks: The atomic base and every tagged constructor map to exactly its source operator.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The definition selects a particular occurrence: in the nested conditional example it is the second conditional. Inductive formation gives existence, unique readability gives uniqueness, so the recursive assignment is a function on non-atomic formulas.
samples.checks: The parse, occurrence number, non-atomic domain, reference, existence argument and uniqueness argument are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Formula names depend on their main operator. Defined operators are only abbreviations and need no separate proof cases; the table lists the atomic, connective and quantified types with examples.
samples.checks: The defined-operator qualification, all table rows, truth-constant tags, formula examples, caption and label are retained.

source_observations: The Marathi main-operator term is explicitly tied to the unique outermost constructor occurrence, not to semantic importance.
The definition's codomain consists of occurrences rather than symbol types, and the translation preserves that distinction.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The table preserves the source's mixed placement of some closing parentheses outside inline math delimiters because the rendered examples and formal bytes are otherwise unchanged.
